title: US Wholesale Inflation Picks Up to Fastest Pace Since 2022
summary:
US wholesale inflation climbed in October from a year earlier at the fastest pace since 2022, adding to evidence of persistent price pressures throughout the economy.
Tani Fukui, Senior Director of Economic & Market Strategy at MetLife Investment Management, discusses consumer outlook and reacts to October PPI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Patterson: For now, Iran has won the war
summary: With the Iran war appearing to de-escalate, energy-market pressure may linger. Iran could retain greater influence over the Strait of Hormuz, keeping shipping and insurance costs elevated even as oil flows resume. Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders and Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson join Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about their new book “Investment Wisdom,” how higher fuel and refined-product costs may feed inflation, complicate the Fed’s path and weigh on the economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stocks Slide as Tech Concerns Linger Despite Rates Relief
summary: US equities fell Friday as investors continue to evaluate the merits of the AI trade, even as wholesale inflation data helped ease fears of an outsized interest-rate hike.

title: Finance Experts Reveal Lessons for Investors
summary: In a world of 24/7 trading, options and investing apps, Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders and Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson join Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about their new book, “Investment Wisdom for Our Friends and Loved Ones: Timeless Lessons from Today’s Top Finance Experts.” They share timeless advice: start early, harness the power of compounding, and know the difference between investing and gambling. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed's Collins Says Additional Policy Tightening Is Appropriate
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins says recent data show inflation is too high and broadening. Speaking with Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Collins adds that because of the increasing inflation risks, more rate tightening is needed. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic IPO Share Orders From China Are Said to Be Rebuffed
summary: Institutional investors based in mainland China and Hong Kong have been excluded from placing orders in Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, highlighting the sensitivities around an industry both Washington and Beijing consider strategic.

title: Raw Sugar Heads for Weekly Rise With India, Brazil in Focus
summary: Raw sugar futures headed for a weekly gain, capping a volatile week as traders looked for signals on the scale and timing of potential imports by India and the state of the weather in Brazil, the world’s top producer.

title: Wall Street Regulator Finra Moves to Give Industry Bigger Role
summary: The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority wants to give the industry it helps regulate a bigger role in its oversight, proposing the first major shakeup in decades to the Wall Street watchdog’s governing board.

title: Senegal Picks Deloitte to Audit Debt as It Seeks IMF Loan Pact
summary: Senegal selected Deloitte to audit its public debt, according to people familiar with the matter, taking a step toward meeting conditions for a proposed $2.2 billion International Monetary Fund program.

title: New Corporate Speak Is Shaped By AI
summary: Corporate managements are using new euphemisms for job cuts or hiring freezes far more in the age of AI, as technology-enabled headcount reductions increasingly draw public ire and pushback from politicians, bloomberg Opinion columnist Jonathan Levin says. As a result, company leaders are leaning on vague talking points about “efficiency,” “automation” and, yes, “delayering.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed’s Logan Seeks Clearer Separation of Market Operations
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Lorie Logan called for the US central bank to separate assets purchased for market-functioning purposes from the ones it holds for monetary-policy operations. “One way to keep market functioning purchases from providing undesired stimulus would be for the FOMC to hold the purchased securities in a separate account and commit to sell them as soon as possible,” Logan said Friday at a bank funding conference co-hosted by the Dallas Fed.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ukraine Hits Ninth Russian Oil Refinery Since Start of November
summary: Ukraine continued its campaign of near daily strikes on Russian oil assets, hitting a major refinery in the Volga region on Friday after the latest round of US-mediated peace talks between the two nations ended earlier this week.

title: Russian Diesel Exports Drop as Ukraine Renews Refinery Attacks
summary: Russian diesel exports slumped at the start of November as renewed Ukrainian attacks on refineries threatened to curb fuel output, even as stronger dirty-fuel shipments lifted the country’s overall oil-product flows.
